current_example.problem: Find, in radians to two decimal places, the argument of $z=-\sqrt{3}-\textrm{i}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226152/assets/0095750158d9a296c9950c2d753ffe820735298c96cdf4de23aef0747862658d.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the third quadrant of the complex plane. Therefore $\pi<        \arg(z)<        \dfrac{3\pi}{2}.$ If $\alpha$ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})=\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta=\arg(z) = \pi +\dfrac\pi 6 = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}.
$$
